original_question: Find the asymptotic value of vgen(n), the minimum number of distinct vectors spanned by an n-point planar set in general position, meaning no three points are collinear and no four are cocircular.
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 39, together with the immediately preceding definition of v(P), v(n), and v_gen(n); the general-position hypothesis is defined earlier in Section 3 just before Problem 8.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact open problem the paper isolates: the asymptotic behavior of v_gen(n) for planar point sets in general position. It also correctly includes the intended general-position condition (no three collinear, no four cocircular) and asks for an asymptotic, not exact, determination.
missing_details: The paper works in the Euclidean plane R^2, so the ambient space should be stated explicitly.
The paper defines the vector-counting function first: v(P) is the number of distinct vectors determined by pairs of points of P, equivalently v(P)=|{p-q : p,q in P, p!=q}|.
The minimization defining v_gen(n) should be written explicitly: v_gen(n)=min{v(P) : P subset R^2, |P|=n, P in general position}.

To make 'spanned vectors' fully unambiguous, one should note that a pair p,q contributes the vectors p-q and q-p; this is a vector problem, not merely a direction-counting or distance-counting problem.
The asymptotic question is about the order of growth of v_gen(n) as n tends to infinity.
refined_question: Let P be a finite subset of R^2, and define v(P):=|{p-q : p,q in P, p!=q}|, the number of distinct vectors determined by ordered pairs of distinct points of P. Define v_gen(n):=min{v(P) : P subset R^2, |P|=n, and P has no three collinear points and no four cocircular points}. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of v_gen(n) as n -> infinity.
justification: This paper is a survey, and the closest official formulation to your draft is the final open problem on distinct vectors in general position. In Section 9, the author introduces the distinct-vector variant by defining v(P) and v(n), then specializes to v_gen(n) for sets in general position, and immediately states Problem 39: find the asymptotic value of v_gen(n). The phrase 'general position' is not redefined there; its exact meaning is supplied earlier in Section 3 before Problem 8 as 'no three points are collinear and no four points are cocircular.' Your draft already captures the main intent, but it leaves implicit the formal definition of v(P) as a set of difference vectors in R^2 and the exact minimization that defines v_gen(n).
